claims.text: The as-processed (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a large caloric response.
The as-processed alloy has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack.
A controlled heat treatment can precipitate a fine, ductile secondary phase in the alloy.
The heat treatment will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale ductile precipitates in the matrix.
The precipitates will hinder crack initiation.
The precipitates will hinder crack propagation by acting as microstructural barriers.
Engineering the precipitate size and distribution will minimize interference with the entropy changes responsible for the caloric response.
The heat-treated alloy will have greater resistance to cracking than the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy will have improved load-bearing integrity relative to the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy's adiabatic temperature change will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The heat-treated alloy's isothermal entropy change will remain comparable to that of the untreated alloy.
The proposed benefit applies under magnetic-field and pressure-field operation typical of solid refrigeration and within the alloy's active caloric temperature range.
The heat-treated and untreated samples will be tested under identical conditions as intervention and control groups.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement of at least 25% in mechanical integrity will falsify the hypothesis.
A decline of more than 10% in either adiabatic temperature change or isothermal entropy change will falsify the hypothesis.
